head: 53d6f31
target: AGENTS.md sets the maintenance contract for the one plugin tree shared by Claude Code, Factory Droid, and Codex: selftest after skills/ or hooks/ changes, manifest validation, a version bump so cached installs see changes, dirname-$0 hook root-finding instead of CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, and the Codex trust rerun after hooks.json edits.
incidental: README.md — documents install, opt-in, and update behavior the code already has

questions.prompt: AGENTS.md keeps one plugin tree serving Claude Code, Factory Droid, and Codex. Why one tree instead of a copy per harness?

options.label: The git pre-push hook only works when a repository has a single plugin tree
All three harnesses read the same .claude-plugin/ and hooks/hooks.json layout, so one shared copy cannot drift the way per-harness copies can
The marketplace registration allows only one plugin.json per repository

key_points: all three harnesses consume the same manifest and hooks.json layout, so there is nothing per-harness to duplicate
one copy is identical for every harness by construction; per-harness copies drift apart
harness differences live in the harnesses, not in copies of the tree

questions.prompt: You fix a bug in the skill's scripts, push it, and never touch version in .claude-plugin/plugin.json. What do existing installs see?

options.label: The pre-push hook blocks the push itself until the version is bumped
The session-start hook pushes the new scripts into every install at the next session
Nothing changes: Claude Code and Codex serve installs from their version-keyed cache, so the fix never reaches users until the version is bumped

key_points: Claude Code and Codex cache the plugin keyed on the version field
a change without a version bump stays invisible to existing installs
the fix reaches users only after a bump and a plugin update

questions.prompt: AGENTS.md forbids hook scripts from reading CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT from the environment and has them find the plugin root with dirname "$0" instead. What does that boundary protect, and from what?

options.label: It keeps root resolution independent of the harness environment: in Droid, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is a placeholder inside hook processes, so the script's own location is the only reliable path to the real install
It stops a malicious repository from pointing the hooks at substitute scripts through an environment variable
It keeps hooks from resolving against Claude Code's plugin cache directory, which moves on every update

key_points: in Droid hook processes CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT holds a placeholder, not the install path
the script's own location ($0) resolves to the true plugin root in every harness
an environment lookup would silently run hooks from a wrong or missing path on Droid

questions.prompt: You add a new hook event by editing hooks/hooks.json. Which of these hold? Pick all that apply.

options.label: Codex skips the plugin's hooks until the new hooks.json is trusted, so an edit that does not announce the rerun leaves Codex users running without the plugin's hooks
Editing hooks/guard or hooks/session-start also invalidates trust, because the hash covers the hook scripts' contents
scripts/codex-trust-hooks writes the same trust entries the Codex TUI writes when a user approves the hooks
Droid and Claude Code users must rerun a trust step too, since all three harnesses share hooks.json

key_points: trust keys on the hooks.json definition hash; editing a hook script's body does not change it
untrusted hooks are skipped, so an unannounced hooks.json edit silently disables the plugin's hooks for Codex users
codex-trust-hooks and TUI approval write the same trust entries
the trust rerun is Codex-only; the other harnesses pick the edit up without a trust step

questions.prompt: AGENTS.md requires running scripts/selftest after any change under skills/ or hooks/. What does that rule protect against, and what does selftest exercise that a quick manual check in one harness would miss?
key_points: one shared tree means an edit lands in all three harnesses at once, so a check in one harness proves nothing about the other two
selftest drives the push gate through a real git push into a bare remote, not a simulation
it feeds the guard each harness's tool name, so per-harness matching regressions are caught before install

questions.prompt: A fourth harness, Amp, adopts own-your-diff and reads the same .claude-plugin/ and hooks/hooks.json layout as the existing three. Which of these follow from the AGENTS.md contract? Pick all that apply.

options.label: Support goes into the existing tree; no Amp-specific copy of skills/ or hooks/ is added
Hooks need an Amp-specific branch for finding the plugin root, since dirname "$0" only works in the three known harnesses
Selftest should feed the guard Amp's tool name so its push attempts are covered
The version in .claude-plugin/plugin.json must be bumped for the change to reach installs

key_points: the tree is harness-agnostic, so the same single copy serves Amp
per-harness guard coverage comes from feeding selftest each harness's tool name, so Amp's name joins that list
$0-based root finding works wherever the hook file itself runs, so no new branch is needed
any change installs must pick up ships with a version bump
